title: Cubs Land Japanese Star Teruaki Sato for $120 Million as a Pre-Thanksgiving Free-Agent Rush Sweeps MLB — With a Possible Lockout Looming Dec. 1
excerpt: Teruaki Sato agreed to a six-year, $120 million deal with the Chicago Cubs, Freddy Peralta landed a five-year, $125 million contract with the Baltimore Orioles, and Kaima Taira chose Toronto for $80 million as teams rushed to sign players before Thanksgiving and a possible Dec. 1 lockout.
content:
CHICAGO — The Chicago Cubs spent nearly a quarter of a billion dollars in about 12 hours. Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato agreed to a six-year, $120 million contract with the Cubs on Tuesday, a day after the club landed left-hander Trevor Rogers on a five-year, $120 million deal.

Sato, a two-time Central League MVP, won the Triple Crown for the Hanshin Tigers in 2026 — a .306 average, 39 home runs and 106 RBIs in 143 games. The 27-year-old is expected to play corner outfield in Chicago, filling one of the voids left by Seiya Suzuki and Ian Happ.

The Baltimore Orioles answered the loss of Rogers by landing their own ace. Former Milwaukee and Tampa Bay right-hander Freddy Peralta agreed to a five-year, $125 million contract with Baltimore, including a $10 million signing bonus and $23 million annual salaries with no opt-outs. Peralta shook off a rough first half with the New York Mets to deliver a strong two months in Tampa Bay, and he will headline a rotation that also includes Kyle Bradish, Shane Baz and Brandon Young.

The Toronto Blue Jays finally landed a significant acquisition, agreeing to a five-year, $80 million contract with Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira, with an opt-out after the third season. The 27-year-old tossed 146 innings with a 1.36 ERA for the Seibu Lions in his return to the rotation after a couple of years in the bullpen.

The rest of Tuesday's rush included left-hander Kris Bubic agreeing to a one-year, $17.5 million deal with the Cleveland Guardians, outfielder Tyrone Taylor agreeing to a two-year, $17 million deal with the Chicago White Sox after hitting .279 this season, infielder Ha-Seong Kim agreeing to a one-year, $5 million deal with the Detroit Tigers, and veteran catcher Tyler Stephenson staying with the Cincinnati Reds on a three-year, $30 million contract. The New York Yankees finalized one-year deals with left-handed relievers Brent Suter ($4 million) and Tim Hill ($2.25 million).

The rush followed a huge weekend: two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with the Mets on Sunday, and the Mets also came to terms on a one-year deal with first baseman Paul Goldschmidt on Monday. The hot stove was lit just days after the Milwaukee Brewers hoisted the franchise's first World Series championship trophy.

With Rogers, Peralta and Taira off the board, Michael King is now the top starting pitcher remaining on the market. Teams are pushing to finish business before Thanksgiving — and before the current labor deal expires Dec. 1, when a lockout could freeze transactions. On Tuesday, Major League Baseball dropped its demand for an escrow provision that was part of its salary-cap proposal, saying instead that any overage or underpayment under a 50-50 revenue split would be accounted for in future seasons.

Sources: MLB Trade Rumors, Nov. 25, 2026; USA Today, Nov. 24, 2026; ESPN, Nov. 25, 2026; TSN, Nov. 24, 2026; Kiner's Korner, Nov. 24, 2026.
